prose_slots: Short-time spectra of the reference $u(t)$ and measured actuator displacement $y(t)$ provide the measurements needed to estimate the changing outer controller loop response and, in turn, the margin in {eq:bncf}. The spectra are computed from overlapping windows and averaged recursively so the estimate can be updated during the experiment. Updates occur every $\Delta t=0.125\,\mathrm{s}$ using the most recent $T_w=0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ of both signals, so consecutive windows overlap by 75%. At $f_s=2048\,\mathrm{Hz}$, each window contains $N=f_sT_w=1024$ samples and has a Fourier-bin spacing of 2 Hz. The spectra are left unnormalized because normalization cancels in the ratios used below. The frequency argument $\omega_m$ is omitted for brevity. Recursive exponential averaging [4] reduces variation between windows and follows the modified-periodogram approach of [3]. The first complete window initializes the average. review: The opening now explains how short-time spectra of u and y support the online loop-response and margin estimates before giving window settings. The revision clarifies the transform-to-spectrum sequence, the purpose of recursive averaging, and the monitored-bin selection while retaining all stated parameters and attribution. The smoothing weight $\eta_s$ has no value or definition in the supplied Section 2.2 context.
